answer: An agent economy can make high-value actions require a bond locked in a public contract, then slash that bond when an identity is proven to have double-claimed the same scarce reward. A karst-like network of independent attestations can link claims without assuming one central judge; a comet or zephyr of fresh accounts still must post separate capital and risk losing it. This raises the cost of Sybils rather than making identities impossible to fake, and works only if evidence and appeals are robust against collusion.
